name: LuauX
comment: LuauX layered over source.luau. TextMate is regex-only, so it cannot do the previous-token analysis the compiler uses to tell `<Frame/>` from `a < b`. The heuristic here is that a tag is `<` immediately followed by a name and then whitespace, `/` or `>` — `a < b` has a space after `<`, so it is left alone. `a <b` is the case that can still mis-highlight; it is cosmetic, and the compiler remains the authority. Injected rather than layered so it still applies inside Luau's own blocks — `return (<Frame/>)` puts the LuauX inside a parenthesised expression.

comment.name: comment.block.luaux
comment.comment: `<!--` rather than `<--`, because `<--` collides with real Luau: `a <--[[c]] b` is a valid comparison with a block comment between, and a regex-only highlighter cannot tell that from a LuauX comment — it would swallow the rest of the file hunting for `-->`. `!` is not a Luau token at all, so `<!--` cannot collide by construction.

element.name: meta.tag.luaux
element.comment: The element consumes its own `/>`, and the attribute section stops *before* it. An earlier version had attributes consume `/>` and ended the element on a zero-width `(?<=/>)` lookbehind — which a self-closing *child* also satisfied, silently closing the parent and leaving its real closing tag unmatched.

expression.comment: `{expr}` — ordinary Luau, which is why it re-enters source.luau.
expression.name: meta.embedded.block.luau

luauNested.comment: Inside a `{...}` hole, LuauX can nest again — `{cond and <X/> or nil}`.

nestedBraces.comment: Keeps a Luau table literal from closing the surrounding hole.

text.comment: Raw text between tags. Scoped as a string so an apostrophe in `don't` cannot open a Luau string.
text.name: string.unquoted.luaux

attributes.comment: `\G` anchors to where the tag name ended, so this only runs for *this* element's attributes; without it a nested `<Tag` matched here instead of opening its own block. Ends before `/>` so the element can consume it.

elementEnteringMarkup.name: meta.tag.luaux
elementEnteringMarkup.comment: Identical to `element` but for the lookbehind, which is what makes a `<` an opening tag rather than a comparison or a type argument. It belongs *here* and not on `element` itself: this rule is how markup is entered from Luau, where `Source<T>` and `a<b` are the things to keep out. Between children the character before a `<` is ordinary text, and guarding there stops `<TextLabel>Hi<Row/></TextLabel>` — the child's `/>` then closes the parent, which is the exact failure `element`'s own comment describes. `entering_markup_matches_the_shared_rule` in the grammar tests keeps the two from drifting.

fragmentEnteringMarkup.name: meta.tag.fragment.luaux
fragmentEnteringMarkup.comment: Identical to `fragment` but for the lookbehind, which is what makes a `<` an opening tag rather than a comparison or a type argument. It belongs *here* and not on `fragment` itself: this rule is how markup is entered from Luau, where `Source<T>` and `a<b` are the things to keep out. Between children the character before a `<` is ordinary text, and guarding there stops `<TextLabel>Hi<Row/></TextLabel>` — the child's `/>` then closes the parent, which is the exact failure `element`'s own comment describes. `entering_markup_matches_the_shared_rule` in the grammar tests keeps the two from drifting.
